eval.description: Anthropic internal agent environments that ask a model to improve machine-learning code across six task families: kernel optimization, time-series forecasting, text-based RL scaffolding, small LLM training speedups, quadruped RL, and building a compiler for a novel language. Cards score each task with its own metric (speedup, MSE or normalized score, RL score, or unit-test pass rate) against expert baselines used for ASL / AI R&D rule-outs. Dataset and runner are lab-internal.
eval.summary: Measures how well AI agents improve machine-learning code, compared with expert human results.
eval.saturatedReason: Claude Opus 4.6 system cards treat most Suite 1 tasks as saturated for the ASL-4 rule-out.

versions.changes: Six task families as described in Anthropic Claude 4 and later system cards. Opus 4.6 cards treat most Suite 1 tasks as saturated for ASL-4 rule-out.

scores.description: Best or average speedup vs a baseline implementation (kernels and LLM training tasks).
Forecast MSE on the time-series task. Cards also report score = exp(-mse/30).
Score on text-based RL scaffolding or quadruped continuous-control variants (thresholds are task-specific).
Share of basic or complex compiler tests passed on the novel-compiler task.

metrics.description: Best-run or average speedup as reported for kernel or LLM-training variants. Other Suite 1 tasks use mse, rl_score, or pass_rate instead; compare only within a task.
Time-series forecasting MSE (often the hard variant).
Best score on text-based RL or quadruped RL variants.
Mean pass rate on novel-compiler basic or complex tests.
